title: All Palindrome Partitions
statement: A calligrapher wants to cut a lowercase word s into consecutive pieces so that every piece reads the same forwards and backwards. Given s, return every possible way to do this. Each way (a partition) is a list of the pieces in left-to-right order, and joining the pieces in order must reproduce s exactly. Return the list of all partitions, sorted lexicographically: compare two partitions element by element as lists of strings (Python's default list comparison). If s is the empty string, return [[]] (one partition with no pieces). Every single character is a palindrome, so a non-empty s always has at least one partition.
hints: At each position you must decide where the current piece ends. What technique explores every choice of cut point and can undo a choice that led down one branch before trying the next?

Backtrack on the start index: try every end such that s[start:end] is a palindrome, append that piece to a path list, recurse from end, then pop the piece off. When start == len(s), record a copy of the path (path[:]) — recording the live list or skipping the pop corrupts later partitions.

def backtrack(start): if start == len(s): results.append(path[:]); return. Otherwise for end in range(start+1, len(s)+1): piece = s[start:end]; if piece == piece[::-1]: path.append(piece); backtrack(end); path.pop(). Call backtrack(0), then results.sort() gives the required lexicographic element-by-element order.
